newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps fall, CFDs dip 8 cts, mogas down $1.50.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps fall, CFDs dip 8 cts, mogas down $1.50.

text.p: European oil swaps slipped lower on Friday in reaction to gains on Thursday and in line with weaker Brent crude futures. But activity was thin with much of Europe on holiday.
Brent CFDs sank about eight cents for next week's dates despite jump in the value of prompt Brent cargoes on Thursday.
Next week was valued at 20 cents under October with the following three weeks at 21 cents, 20 cents and 20 cents under respectively.
Next week traded at 20 cents under while the following two weeks were traded as a spread at parity.
The flat weekly CFD structure was in contrast to most other areas of the market. Monthly CFDs against the IPE remain in contango as do heavy fuel swaps which eased $1 a tonne.
August was valued around $94.50, pressured by looming Russian exports. September was about $1 and October another $1 higher.
Gasoline slipped $1.50 a tonne to $200 for September and $190 for October although the only trade reported was at $226.50 for physical barges.
"The heat is going to continue to come out of the market over the next few days," said a refiner referring to recent levels of barges as high as $240.

Naphtha fell $1 a tonne to $188.50 for September amid poor demand and falling Brent. "The (naphtha) cracks are also under pressure so any move in Brent is being matched on outright prices," said a trader.
Gas oil swaps were little changed despite the weaker tone on IPE gas oil futures.
Jet premiums were unchanged following several days of weaker prices on the fourth quarter.
